newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek banks stop trade on prospect of depo tax.
newsitem.headline: Greek banks stop trade on prospect of depo tax.

text.p: Greek banks stopped quoting prices and trading in tenors over one month on reports of plans by the socialist government to impose a new tax on interbank depos, dealers said.

"Banks are dealing in short periods up to a month because there is uncertainty and anger over reports that the government will impose a new tax on interbank depos," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank.
Traders said they were trading overnight and tomorrow-next funds to close out positions.
"We are not engaging in trading for periods over one month because we suspect that the new tax, if true, will go into effect January 1, 1997," said another dealer at a foreign bank.

Officials at the national economy ministry and the finance ministry told Reuters that National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou was at a cabinet meeting on the 1997 budget and was not available for comment.
Ecu/drachma had firmed to 303.70/80 on light ecu buying interest from abroad. It was trading at 303.30/40 on Monday afternoon. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
